title: The Merchant and the Two Sharpers
logline: Two cheats join a rich merchant s caravan to rob him, but each secretly poisons the other to keep the whole prize, and the merchant travels on unharmed without ever learning the full story.
moral: Whoever digs a pit for his partner falls into it himself: greed and betrayal destroy the traitors, and the honest man is saved without lifting a finger.
tone: Dry comic irony. The two cheats are a double act (smooth leader, clumsy copycat) played as mirror images; the deaths are quick, bloodless and discreet; the merchant is warm and a little naive, and his ending is quiet relief rather than triumph.

beats.summary: A rich merchant of Sindah with many goods to sell in another city.
He loads his camels and sets out on the long road.
Two cheats hear of the journey and decide to travel with him.
They pass behind a palm and come out dressed as merchants, with two tiny bundles.
The merchant welcomes them; behind his back, a wink.
At the first rest stop they plot to take his goods and be rich.
Each hides a second idea: why share?
The two secret thoughts are shown side by side: identical.
The first drips poison into a bowl and offers it with a smile.
The second does the same trick, clumsier, and the tableau shows two smiles, two bowls, two hidden vials.
They eat what they gave each other, each watching the other swallow.
The poison strikes both; mutual discovery; both fall.
Next morning the merchant finds them and reads the clues.
He understands they were never honest companions.
Safe, he takes what they left and continues his journey.
Crossed arrows over the two bowls: each died by the food the other prepared.

sets.description: Reuses the planned name desertRoad (AN-095) with a city-edge option. World 2400 x 1230, ground y 900, skyCycle sky. City edge x 0-620: ochre wall top y 520 with crenellations, gate arch centred x 330 (opening 200 wide x 300 tall, navy inside), two domes and one tower behind (top y 260). Sandy road band y 900-960 running the full width with a milestone every 500. Three dune ridges (parallax 0.4, 0.6, 0.8) in yellow and orange with red dot shading. Palms at x 760, 1640 (the wipe palm, trunk 60 wide, drawn in FRONT of actors) and 2200. Low mud wall x 1340-1560, top y 770 (the cheats hiding place). Tiny far city silhouette on the horizon at x 2250.

New reusable night/day campsite. World 2200 x 1230, ground y 900, skyCycle sky with dayCycle().night tint on the land. Left to right: big striped tent x 150-560 (peak y 520, door flap at x 420 that can lift), small tent x 600-800 (peak y 640, liftable flap), campfire x 930 (states unlit, lit, dead with a smoke thread), two cushions at x 860 and 990, camel line x 1080 and 1290 on a back plane y 880, palm x 1400, three road posts x 1300-1480, rock outcrop x 1500-1680 (top y 700, grey with blue dot shading) that screens the right part from the tents, the cheats mat x 1700-2060 (red carpet 360 x 18 with yellow fringe, top at y 900) with a small oil lamp at x 1880, and a dune lip directly behind the mat (crest y 880, 30 high) that hides anything lying behind it. Far tiny road over the last dune at x 2000-2200, y 760, for the departing caravan.

props.description: camelLoad: cloth bolts (cylinders 120 x 34 in red, blue and yellow with a spiral end and two stripe bands), sacks (the planned sack, 70 x 90), a treasure chest (110 x 80, brown with yellow bands, lid angle 0..1 with glow), saddle frame with ropes; the same items lie in a pile on the ground or sit on a camel hump. Also the two tiny bindles (planned bindle: 40 px bundle on a 110 stick).

smallBowl (planned name) with options: rim colour (A yellow, B red), fill 0..1 of brown stew, steam (3 wavy lines), badge (green dot with a darker ring on the rim = poisoned, can pulse), upturned state. Bowl 90 wide x 46 tall. Bowl B is the same drawing with a red rim. Served from the planned foodTray (brass tray 200 wide).

poisonVial: small green glass bottle 22 x 46 with a cork and a white highlight; fields cork (on/off), tilt, level 0..1; drops are 6 px green teardrops. No skull or text on the bottle; the S.label "POISON" names it.

subtitles.ar: كان تاجر غني يعيش في مدينة اسمها سندة،|ويملك بضائع كثيرة يريد بيعها في مدينة أخرى.|جهز جماله وحمل عليها الأقمشة والأشياء الثمينة،|ثم انطلق في رحلة طويلة عبر الطريق.
subtitles.en: A wealthy merchant|in a city named Sindah|packed cloth and valuable goods on camels|and set out to trade in another city.

subtitles.ar: سمع رجلان محتالان عن رحلته، فاتفقا على السفر معه.|حملا بعض البضائع الصغيرة، وتظاهرا بأنهما تاجران مثله.|رحب الرجل بهما، لأنه ظن أنهما يريدان التجارة والصحبة في الطريق.
subtitles.en: Two cheats heard of his journey and joined him,|carrying a few goods and pretending to be merchants.|He welcomed their company.

subtitles.ar: عند أول مكان توقفوا فيه للراحة، جلس المحتالان وحدهما.|قال أحدهما للآخر: «هذا الرجل يحمل مالًا كثيرًا.|إذا أخذنا بضاعته فسوف نصبح أغنياء».|وافق صاحبه، وبدآ يخططان لخداعه.
subtitles.en: At the first rest stop,|the cheats agreed to steal the merchant’s valuable cargo|and become rich.|They began planning the theft.

subtitles.ar: لكن كل واحد منهما أخفى فكرة أخرى.|فكر الأول: «لماذا أقسم المال مع صاحبي؟|لو تخلصت منه لأخذت كل شيء».|وفي الوقت نفسه كان الثاني يفكر في خيانة الأول بالطريقة نفسها.
subtitles.en: Secretly, each thought:|“Why share the wealth?|If I get rid of my partner I can keep everything.”|Both planned to betray the other.

subtitles.ar: أخذ المحتال الأول طعامًا ووضع فيه سمًا،|ثم قدمه إلى صاحبه متظاهرًا بالكرم.|أما المحتال الثاني ففعل الشيء نفسه،|وأعد طعامًا مسمومًا للأول، من غير أن يعرف خطة شريكه.
subtitles.en: The first poisoned food|and offered it to his companion, pretending generosity.|The second independently|prepared poisoned food for the first.

subtitles.ar: جلس الاثنان يأكلان ما قدماه لبعضهما.|لم يشك أي واحد منهما في أن الطعام الذي أمامه مسموم،|لأنه كان مشغولًا بفكرة نجاح خطته الخاصة.|وبعد وقت قصير أصابهما السم وماتا.
subtitles.en: They ate the food they had exchanged.|Neither suspected the meal before him was poisoned,|each preoccupied with his own scheme.|Soon both died.

subtitles.ar: لاحظ التاجر غيابهما الطويل،|فخرج يبحث عنهما بين الخيام وعلى الطريق.|وجدهما ميتين في مكان بعيد.|وعندما عرف ما تركاه وراءهما، فهم أنهما لم يكونا رفيقي سفر صادقين.
subtitles.en: Noticing their long absence,|the merchant searched|and found them dead.|From what they left behind, he understood they had not been honest companions.

subtitles.ar: نجا التاجر من السرقة|من غير أن يعرف كل التفاصيل التي دارت بين الرجلين.|وأخذ البضائع التي تركاها، ثم تابع طريقه.|أما المحتالان فقد مات كل واحد منهما بسبب طعام أعده له الآخر.
subtitles.en: The merchant escaped the theft|without knowing every detail,|took the goods they left and continued his journey.|Each cheat had died from the food prepared by the other.

new_assets.name: camel
new_assets.description: One-humped comic camel for any caravan or desert story. About 400 wide x 370 tall at s 1 (hump top 300, head top 370), feet at (x, y), x at body centre, facing dir. Pose fields: ph, amp (walk; pacing gait, the two legs of one side move together), kneel 0..1 (0-0.5 front legs fold, 0.5-1 rear legs fold; body ends 120 lower), headTurn 0..1 (head swings back over the shoulder), neck -1..1 (down to graze / up), chew, talk (grumble, lower lip), ears, tailSwish, load (array of cargo items drawn on the hump), pal (0 sand, 1 brown, 2 white), plus the shared acting fields.
new_assets.implementation: One function in Library/cast, built like the deer/lion: body = rounded box 230 x 120 in sand with red-dot shading on the belly, hump = half ellipse 120 x 70 on top, neck = two tapered quads forming a shallow S (60 wide at the base, 34 at the head) so headTurn and neck are simple angle changes at two joints, head = rounded wedge 110 x 60 with a split upper lip, big lidded eye (eye2 from core/helpers so gaze/lid work), small round ears, four two-segment legs 150 long with knobbly knee circles and wide two-toed feet (walk() drives ph; for the pace gait give the same-side legs the same phase), tuft tail on swing(). kneel folds the lower leg segments under the body and translates the body down. Wrap with acting() in registry.js and add catalogue poses stand, walk, kneel, loaded, head turned.

new_assets.name: desertRoad
new_assets.description: The planned desert travel strip (AN-095) with a city-edge option for Sindah, a hiding wall, a foreground wipe palm and a far city (dimensions under sets).
new_assets.implementation: Flat polygons baked with bake(): sky by skyCycle, three dune ridge polygons with K halftone dot fills, road band, wall and gate from rectangles and an arc, domes as half circles. Palm = the planned palmTree(ctx, x, baseY, {h, lean, fronds}) if it exists by then, otherwise a ringed tapered trunk and 7 frond arcs. Draw the wipe palm trunk after the actors.

new_assets.name: desertCamp
new_assets.description: Campsite with two tents, fire, cushions, camel line, palm, a screening rock, a carpet mat and a dune lip, usable at dusk, night and morning (dimensions under sets).
new_assets.implementation: Tents = triangles with striped panels (red and white, blue and white) and a flap quad whose angle is a parameter; fire = 3 log rects and a flame polygon flickering from K.noise; rock = irregular polygon with dot shading; mat = rect with fringe ticks; dune lip = a ground-coloured polygon drawn AFTER the fallen figures so it hides them. Bake three versions for dusk, night and morning tint (or tint the land with dayCycle().night at draw time).

new_assets.name: camelLoad (cloth bolts, chest, sacks, bindle)
new_assets.description: The cargo items listed under props, each a small function, usable on the ground or on a camel.
new_assets.implementation: Rounded rects and ellipses with stripe bands; chest lid rotates about its back edge with a yellow halftone glow and 3 K star glints when open.

new_assets.name: smallBowl (rim colour, steam, poison badge) and poisonVial
new_assets.description: The planned smallBowl extended with rim colour, steam, a pulsing green badge and an upturned state; a small green vial with cork and drops.
new_assets.implementation: Bowl = half ellipse with a coloured rim stroke; badge = green circle r 9 with a ring, scale pulsed by pulse(); steam = three sine paths with alpha from K.noise; vial = rounded rect + neck + cork; drops fall with fallY and make ripple rings in the stew.

new_assets.name: poison face tint
new_assets.description: Green halftone dots that climb a person s face from the chin to the brow over about 0.6 s (used once, 124.3).
new_assets.implementation: After drawing the person, clip to a circle at the head centre (figure-local head position times s) and fill a green dot pattern whose top edge rises with t; same idea as the planned "flush" expression, so implement as flush with a colour parameter.

new_assets.name: costume change behind a foreground wipe
new_assets.description: Planned in AN-095: a walker passes behind a foreground palm trunk and comes out in the next costume.
new_assets.implementation: Switch the costume and pal fields at the time the figure s x equals the trunk centre; the trunk (60 wide) is drawn after the actors; figure width at s 1 is 120, so widen the trunk to 130 at body height with a frond clump or let the swap happen under a 2-frame star pop.

owner_questions: The two cheats are given distinct looks and tags "1" and "2" (tall green-robed leader, short red-robed copycat) although the script does not describe them; default: yes.
The deaths are softened: faces turn comic green, both topple backward behind a dune lip, and afterwards only shoes and fallen turbans are shown, never faces or bodies in close view; default: yes.
A comic beat is added at 125.36 where each cheat points at the other and realises the double betrayal just before dying (the script only says the poison struck them and they died); default: keep.
The merchant "understands" from clues invented for the staging: the vials, the green-badged bowls, the fallen false turbans and the plan drawn in the sand; default: keep.

Invented on-screen lettering and labels (RICH MERCHANT, SINDAH, TWO CHEATS, GOODS?, TA-DA!, RICH!, ALL MINE!, SAME IDEA!, POISON, DRIP!, GLUG!, CLINK!, URK!, HELLO?, SAFE!, MADE BY 1, MADE BY 2) and the closing box caption "EACH FELL INTO THE TRAP HE SET"; default: keep all.
The LATER card reads "NEXT MORNING..." (the script says only that he noticed their long absence); default: NEXT MORNING...
The cheats first appear as plain rogues and change into merchant costume behind a palm on the word "pretended"; default: yes.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; two baked sets (desertRoad for S1-S4, desertCamp for S5-S16). Use the panel-only shake of the template for the single shake at 124.3.

All three people are the Library person with costume and pal; never draw one-off humans. Use LIFE.t = t for automatic blinks and give explicit lid values only where listed (shock holds use P.noBlink).

The person figure is front-facing only. "Turning his back" in S9/S10 is staged by moving the bowl and both hands to the far side of the body (handLW/handRW), hunching (tip -0.06, sq 0.97) and sending the gaze over the shoulder toward the partner.

Bowl bookkeeping, which carries the whole story: bowl A (yellow rim) is poisoned by sharper 1 and eaten by sharper 2; bowl B (red rim) is poisoned by sharper 2 and eaten by sharper 1. From 102.0 to the end, bowl A sits in front of sharper 2 (x 1960) and bowl B in front of sharper 1 (x 1800). The green badge never leaves a bowl once applied (93.24 and 101.18).
Thought clouds: one at a time except the mirrored pair at 82.8-85.2 and 117.3-122.5; keep figures inside at least 110 px; clouds must not cover the thinkers faces (place above and to the outer side).
Camels never move in unison: offset ph by 0.5 and chew cycles by 0.37 s. Walk positions are functions of t passed to walk() and footfalls() so feet do not slide; the merchant leads at 95 units/s.
Mirror staging: write sharper A s poisoning pose function once and reuse it mirrored for B with a stagger and the clumsy additions.

Sound: narration is continuous with no pause of 0.6 s or more, so every effect sits on a word boundary after a comma or full stop, very quiet (SND master 0.6, gains 0.25 or less) and shorter than 0.15 s; if any effect masks a word in the mix, drop it. The safe gaps are 64.78-65.04, 105.64-105.80 and after 169.24.
Subtitles: use the chunk marks in "subtitles" (verbatim from story/script.json); chunk times come from the first word of each chunk in timing.json.

Fall behind the dune lip: draw order is mat, fallen figures (person lie:1 with lid 1, rotated so the head points away from camera is not possible, so simply translate them down and back by 40 units while lying), then the dune lip polygon, then bowls, vials and turbans in front.
Lettering never covers a face; headlines at least 44 px and labels at least 28 px at 1280x720 scale; no en or em dashes; call S.finish last every frame.
warnings: The camel is a large new character (effort L) and is on screen in 9 of 16 scenes; draw and approve it first on a still sheet.
No narration pause reaches 0.6 s: effects must be very sparse and quiet; the listed sfx times are word boundaries, not true silences.
Poisoning and two deaths in a children s format: staged discreetly (see owner_questions 2 and 3); the owner may want it softer still.

The person figure has no profile or back view; the "back turned" and "back to back" staging depends on hands, gaze and prop placement reading clearly at phone size. Check with stills at 89.7, 103.8 and 83.4.

Sharper B without a beard depends on the merchant preset allowing the beard to be switched off; if not, give him a short grey-brown beard via pal.beard and keep the size difference as the main distinction.
The city name is written SINDAH as in the English script.
